t: Section 212(a)(1)(A)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(1)(A)(i)) is amended by striking “, which shall include infection with the etiologic agent for acquired immune deficiency syndrome,” and inserting a semicolon.

fable.w: This section is a purely textual amendment that removes the HIV-specific language from an inadmissibility ground in the Immigration and Nationality Act. The tempting reading is that the underlying provision involves health determinations made by regulation, but this section itself neither grants nor requires rulemaking, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or consultation with any party outside the federal government. Congress makes the change directly, so no outside party is involved in any federal decision.

It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It is purely a legislative change to statutory text.

opus.w: This section only removes the words about "infection with the etiologic agent for acquired immune deficiency syndrome" from an inadmissibility ground. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision. The underlying INA clause does refer to HHS regulations, but that language is not in this section, which grants no new rulemaking authority and creates no outside participation.

It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory committees, or hearings. The action is taken by Congress through the statute itself, not through a participatory process involving non-federal parties.
qwen_chat.s: Section 212(a)(1)(A)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(1)(A)(i)) is amended by striking “, which shall include infection with the etiologic agent for acquired immune deficiency syndrome,” and inserting a semicolon.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that removing a specific medical exclusion could be seen as a policy change affecting public health, but the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or participation. It is a purely legislative amendment to a statutory list of inadmissible conditions.
